conservation.condition_narrative:
The painting was damaged and treated shortly after it was painted. Carolyn Keck was the conservator who treated it in 1955, and some of her treatment notes are written on the back of the panel. It was lined with wax-resin to linen before mounting to the panel. In addition, the painting was revarnished with B-72 in May of 2001 probably in preparation for sale to Gilcrease museum as indicated by a label stuck to the back of the painting. Winterthur library was contacted (where Keck treatment records are housed) but the librarian was unable to locate any records regarding treatment other than the painting belonged to a gallery at the time the treatment was done by Mrs. Keck. It is unclear why the painting was mounted to a panel. Cursory visual examination reveals a dent in the side of the antelope head and some inpainting there. 
 
DESCRIPTION: 
The painting shows an antelope skull floating in the sky. The flat-topped New Mexico mountain, Pedernal, is in the background. The frame appears to be original to the work and has been painted by the artist to continue the background onto the frame. 
 
CONDITION: 
Examination revealed a small flake of loose blue paint in the sky. The paint on the frame is grubby from handling. 
 
TREATMENT: 
The flake and a few other cracks in the blue sky were consolidated with Aquazol 200 in ethanol and water.

description: A textured, craggy brown antelope skull with large horns floats on the right side of the canvas. Behind the skull is the deep blue form of Pedernal. A sunrise with a glowing white sun and bands of pink and blue sky stretches overhead.
title: Antelope Head with Pedernal
